extracted.intended_audience: BBC staff: editors, journalists, producers and others responsible for editorial content and compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial rules and standards governing how BBC output and representatives must achieve 'due impartiality' across genres, plus mandatory referral requirements and procedural safeguards for content, contributors and use of AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Impartiality means not favouring one side over another and reflecting all relevant sides of the debate. It means not taking sides, reflecting all relevant strands of public debate and challenging them with consistent rigour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impartiality is fundamental to the BBC's purpose and Charter; it underpins trust that the BBC is not being influenced by personal or other agendas in what it broadcasts or publishes. Apply across output and behaviours of people who represent the BBC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due impartiality (standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'due impartiality' means adequate and appropriate to the output, taking account of the subject and nature of the content, the likely audience expectation, and any signposting that may influence that expectation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impartiality should be calibrated to genre, subject and audience; it is not a one-size-fits-all formula and requires judgement. Transparency about how impartiality is achieved and prompt correction of errors are part of meeting due impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflect full range of interests and views
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC needs to be able to portray and include the full range of interests and views across all the audiences it serves. Those views and interests should be reflected fairly and accurately, and the BBC should not be seen to be promoting or revealing opinions of its own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflection should be fair and accurate across output as a whole and over an appropriate timeframe so no significant strand of thought is under-represented or omitted; this may include unpalatable or offensive opinions where omission would affect impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality rests on judgement, not formula
rubrics_metrics.description: Impartiality will always rest on good judgement, rather than any mathematical formula; it contains many elements, such as 'accuracy', 'fairness', 'objectivity', 'open-mindedness' and it always takes account of context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not mechanically balance viewpoints; editorial discussion and judgement are required to apply impartiality correctly for each piece of output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and evidence-based approach
rubrics_metrics.description: A key way to do this is in being fact and evidence based, holding authorities and others to account, on behalf of the public, for what they say and do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factual accuracy and evidence underpin impartiality; objective judgements may be made based on evidence without violating impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to give all views equal weight (avoid false equivalence)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no requirement to give all views equal weight – false equivalence does not achieve impartiality and should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minority views or those less supported by evidence do not need similar prominence or weight to those with more support, prevailing consensus, or better evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highest level of impartiality for news and current affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: The highest level of impartiality is required in news and journalism in all its forms, giving due weight to events, opinion and the main strands of argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audiences expect news, current affairs and factual journalism to meet the highest levels of impartiality and accuracy; references to factual journalism include journalistic content produced outside news/current affairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality allows evidence-based and editorial judgements
rubrics_metrics.description: Achieving impartiality does not preclude making evidence-based judgements or making an editorial judgement to focus scrutiny on a particular position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial focus or scrutiny is permitted where justified by evidence or editorial reasons; such judgements should still be consistent with due impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take account of different political cultures and regional views
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC's output should take account of the different political cultures and structures across the UK and the distinct views of some communities and sections of society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise when main strands of argument differ, especially in the Nations and English Regions, giving them due weight and prominence in UK-wide output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity when artists/entertainers express personal views
rubrics_metrics.description: Audiences expect artists, writers and entertainers to have freedom to explore subjects from a particular perspective and to create content that reflects their own distinctive voice. It must be clear to audiences where personal views are being expressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow creative freedom but signal clearly when personal views are being presented to avoid confusing editorial position with individual expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid endorsing campaigns when highlighting issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Where BBC content highlights issues on which others campaign, care must be taken to avoid endorsing those campaigns, or allowing the BBC to be seen as campaigning to change public policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlighting issues and offering audiences information and choices is allowed, but must not cross into campaigning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying impartiality effectively may mean being transparent in explaining how impartiality is achieved on behalf of all audiences and correcting quickly anything which is wrong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open about editorial decisions where helpful to audiences; correct errors promptly to maintain trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: External activities and speech by BBC representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: External activities and public expressions of opinion, including on social media, may affect perceptions of the BBC's impartiality as much as its output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies differently according to genre and role; staff should consult related guidance (Section 4 Conflicts of Interest, Section 10 Politics and Public Policy, Personal Use of Social Media).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory referral: proposals expressing a particular/singular view on controversial subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptionally, an individual programme or other BBC content which is not part of a series or long-running output may include the expression of a particular or singular view on a 'controversial subject', current public policy or a political issue. Any such proposal must be referred to Chief Adviser Politics to ensure it still meets the requirements of due impartiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such referrals must be made in advance. See cross-reference 2.4.30.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory referral: inviting politicians into non-political output
rubrics_metrics.description: Chief Adviser Politics must be consulted in advance of any proposal to invite a politician to take part in output which would not normally include politicians, political opinions or 'controversial issues', irrespective of whether the proposed contribution is itself 'political'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any offer from a politician to take part in such output must also be referred before it is accepted or declined. See 2.4.31 and Section 10 cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory referral: staff in roles requiring impartiality planning public political expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual in a role requiring impartiality who is intending to express opinions publicly on matters of current public policy, politics or any controversial issue, or taking part in political activity, must inform their line manager in advance, who should consult Chief Adviser Politics if there is a risk to impartiality, or the perception of impartiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See related guidance in Section 4 Conflicts of Interest (4.4.13-4.4.20) and Personal Use of Social Media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory referral: staff intending to seek political nomination
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual who intends to seek nomination as a party candidate for election at national or local level, or intends declaring publicly their independent candidacy, must notify their line manager in advance, who should then consult Chief Adviser Politics before the intention is made public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Section 4 Conflicts of Interest (4.4.21-4.4.23) for further detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory referral: commenting publicly on BBC matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless it is a professional responsibility, any individuals commenting publicly – such as on social media – on BBC matters, stories about the BBC, or issues concerning other broadcasters or broadcasting policy, must consult their line manager in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is to manage risks to perceived impartiality. See 2.4.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory referral: potentially seriously offensive views/language
rubrics_metrics.description: There are some views and language which may cause serious offence, but a failure to reflect them could have implications for the BBC's impartiality; if there is a risk either of causing serious offence or jeopardising impartiality, referral must be made to a senior editorial figure, who should consult Editorial Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senior editorial figure should consider both harm/offence and impartiality risks. See Section 5 Harm and Offence (5.4.24-5.4.36).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory consultation when commissioning drama/entertainment on controversial subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: When commissioning drama, entertainment or cultural output covering matters of current public policy, political or industrial controversy, or other 'controversial subjects', Editorial Policy must be consulted in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to commissioning decisions to ensure due impartiality in non-news genres. See 2.4.33.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior editorial oversight and referral for use of AI
rubrics_metrics.description: A senior editorial figure must be responsible and accountable for overseeing the deployment and continuing use of any Artificial Intelligence (AI). They should seek advice from Editorial Policy, who may consult the AI Risk Advisory Group, before any decision to deploy the AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For independent production companies, proposed use of AI with material impact on audience-facing content should be discussed in the commissioning process; a senior editorial figure within the production team must be responsible for compliance.
